summary: The frozen question meets substantial-target admission: the printed terminal theorem composes actual Profile A and B exclusions, and the two-star theorem has explicit family hypotheses with no I27 antecedent. The manuscript consistently separates the local conditional global theorem, the unconditional structural theorem, the external ordinary corollary, and failed diagnostics. One definition should be made explicit before final acceptance: f(4,3) must denote the maximum sunflower-free family size rather than the forcing threshold.
required_revisions: Define f(4,3) explicitly as the maximum cardinality of a finite four-uniform three-sunflower-free family (if that is the intended convention), so the displayed 54 ≤ f(4,3) ≤ 80 cannot be read as a forcing-threshold statement.

findings.statement: The paper defines G(N) and I(N), but never defines f(4,3). Both maximum-free-size and forcing-threshold conventions occur for sunflower extremal functions; they differ by one, so Corollary 4 should state the intended convention.
findings.disposition: Add one explicit definition near Section 1 or the first occurrence of f(4,3).

findings.statement: The supplied receipts show nontrivial actual-family theorem interfaces: Profile A is excluded from I27, Profile B is excluded, and I27→G80 is proved by composition; the unconditional two-star root quantifies over arbitrary finite four-uniform sunflower-free families.
findings.disposition: Substantial-target admission is supported at the stated same-evaluator axiom-audit assurance level; source closure and prior-art detail remain for later phases.

checks.scope: Conditional versus unconditional quantifiers and admission
checks.method: Read the frozen admission record and exact printed theorem outputs in terminal, two-star and Profile A receipts; compare antecedents with Theorems 1–3 and the abstract.
checks.observation: The expanded terminal proposition has a universally quantified I27 antecedent and conclusion G80; its sunflower predicate allows an arbitrary core and uses a three-element subfamily. The independent_twenty_stars root has four-uniformity, sunflower-freeness, distinct centers, degrees twenty, and no joint center membership, with no I27 input. This matches the manuscript and establishes more than an undischarged A/B implication.

checks.method: Check degree-profile sums and the meanings of finite family, distinct petals, empty core, and extremal-function notation against the literal terminal proposition.
checks.observation: Profile A gives 20+16·19=324=4·81; Profile B gives 40+14·19+18=324. The literal three-element subfamily predicate excludes repetitions and permits empty core as claimed. The undefined f notation leaves a preventable maximum-versus-threshold ambiguity.
